State of Decay 2 is a zombie apocalypse game.  But the real horror here is Microsoft forcing you to log into Xbox Live just to play a game where you're supposedly able to play single player only.

claims.claim: The game features base-building, looting, and community management mechanics.

citations.review_text: One of the best all round zombie survival games out there. There's base-building, melee and ranged combat and a very natural skill progression in which you improve what you use... Run around alot? You get better stamina management, shoot a lot - get better at shooting... Etc.

the first 1-2 hours of the game are amazing, but after you get into the part where you manage "communities"/base, it all goes bad. the gameplay is repetitive, extremely grindy and the combat mechanics are lacking. this game is a logistics simulator, where you also play as a courier and there are so many game mechanics that serve no purpose. if you like grindy games where you have to micro manage everything, knock yourself out with this one

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
+ Sandbox about building communities in zombie apocalypse, ( if you're into games like that with no story and no real end-goal )
+ Base/Outpost management
+ Looting

[h1]Cons:[/h1]
- Game doesn't have any real story campaign, other than you building your own story
- There's no real end-goal other than trying to survive (which is really easy to do unless you max out the difficulty)
- Game get dry real fast, only after few hours, after you've cleared out the map of plague hearts
- No fast-travel between base/outposts(?)
- It's just a sandbox

[h1]Conclusion:[/h1]
The game is kind of fun to play in smaller dosages, but it doesn't keep you hooked if you're not into games where you build and manage your own community in zombie apocalypse with no end-goal other than surviving in sight.

It's not a bad game, not at all. But it got really dry for me after few hours, after clearing my first map from plague hearts and doing busy-work missions just so that those enclaves don't complain if I ignore their missions.
The first SoD was great introduction to this franchise, but this sequel kind of falls flat in not pushing the franchise further and evolving more. SoD2 mostly just adds some quality of life features that the first game lacked.

The only reason I'm giving this game a thumbs down is, because it didn't evolve enough from the first game.
Hopefully the SoD3 (if it ever comes out) will push this franchise further and adds a proper story campaign.
Great survival zombie game with cool community building mechanics
Great game, the base building zombie apocalypse is such a great idea
Great game if you like base management and killing zombies

citations.review_text: Really great zombie game thats fun to play and had huge potential. However it gets held back by its limitations. The coop has a tether so its not great for coop exploring since you need to be close together, and the main purpose of the game limits the fun since all you do is clear plague hearts then move to a new map. Wish the modding scene could change the gameplay and make it a fun survival game where you need to eat and scavenge, but i doubt its possible and mods are limited unless you want cheat mods. Overall its a game with huge potential that gets handicapped by its limitations.

Although not a bad game in itself, it is just not mature enough. 2 items will frustrate the heck out of you when playing multiplayer. 1. shared inventory does not exist. You are with a friend, grab something and put it into the base storage, he cannot see it. You either have to give it to him to put into storage or leave in trunk of vehicle so he can access it. Extremely painful. 2. tethering - just why. Fortunately SoD 3 is suppose to resolve these issues, so just wait for that. But if you want single player, for $5 you can do this one and get used to some of the mechanics.

claims.claim: Companions controlled by AI can behave poorly in combat, such as charging armed hostiles or juggernauts with melee weapons.

citations.review_text: I'm all for games with PERMA DEATH and all when I did something to cause a death. But For me to put my player in a snipe position just for the AI companion to go charging into a building with HOSTILES with guns activity shooting at us.  Naw, i'm done, Its one thing is if its part of the STORY but because the AI made it run in with its BAT like it was gonna do something to three armed hostiles. Done and uninstalling.

Look, i get it, is it survival game.
But the lack of QoL, fact that you cannot have manual saves, and some issues like dumb teammates NPCs, makes it really bad experience.
It seems game is mostly focused on multiplayer, and if you expect (as i do) that you will be building bases with useful NPCs, raiding zombies together and do other stuff... no.

Bases? Too small and limited. Outposts? You can have only few. NPCs? You can only take 1 teammate to combat and they are incredibly stupid. You cannot even see their HP unless you go in menu or switch to them.

Propably the worst part, every stuff costs influence. WHY??? It is extremely difficult to get and you need it for everything - recruiting NPCs, base capture, outpost uprgades.

So, now, after 7 hours, i am uninstalling. I just lost 2 (of my 6 total) NPCs because some juggernout spawned out of nowhere, and my NPC teammate (who cannot be controled) decided to go melee against him and bunch of others.
Loss of NPC is a huge impact, mostly because how expensive it is to actually recruit new one.
This game is not difficult, it is annoying. Everything could be scaled differently - bigger bases, more complex economy, larger teams... you would feel like you are building something.
At this point, nothing really feels like being worth of my time. Nothing feels rewarding.
Heck, you even spend ages driving across the map to do the quest just to find out, to finish the quest you pretty much need to go back.

claims.claim: Zombies spawn randomly and immediately in cleared areas when the player looks away.

citations.review_text:
It's a very good game, everything is great. On higher difficulties, the game is not just difficult and it's still enjoyable. The music is very good. It would be very interesting if some of the lakes had fishing capabilities.
Just one thing that bothers me is that zombies constantly spawn in the most random locations. I get tired of the game. When I go through the path, I clear it, and when I look behind me, it's FULL of zombies AGAIN.

My only want for state of decay 3 is that zombies spawn further away from you. I clear out a parking lot, look away for 5 seconds and look back and a horde has spawned right there. Other than that, no notes. Its a perfect zombie survival game

Enter Side-Mission to kill human NPCs
Said Human NPCs refuse to die no matter how many headshots they take or pummels on the ground.
Restart game.
Clears bug, but lose a precious Teammate because the game resets you right back to the spot with less ammo and he was swarmed to death.
Quit.

There is no excuse for how buggy and glitchy this game is. 

On top of that, the way it handles 'difficulty' is artificial BS at its most egregious!

Spawning an undead horde (and some freaks) out of nowhere is NOT good game design, it's just cheap dopamine satiating BS!! And it wrecks your progress because you'll be preparing for a mission, but than suddenly two ferals, a juggernaut, and an undead horde appear out of nowhere, and if you do survive that attack, you'll need to reload and heal up and hope to God, the game doesn't do it again...it'll do it again!

Instead of throwing 'Curveballs' at me, and admitting that your game design sucks hard, how about you FIX THE GAME UNDEAD LABS!!

To make it worse, the AI is terrible and hardly does anything other than wait on you. And the world wears out its welcome quickly when it just resets itself to where the same zombies you killed and same fences you broke 'magically' return to place.

It all feels like an infinite engagement loop where progression feels hollow, and the tedium sets in fast. 

This is a full-priced sequel, yet it doesn't feel like it improved much at all with the original game.

EDIT: Having pushed through more of the story content and other maps, it's only more painful. The more narrative driven elements help alleviate what is obvious: The game needs a massive overhaul in its end-game loop. Because right now, there is NO incentive to continue beyond the mid-game, especially once the plague hearts are gone. 

More dynamic enclave actions.
More story-based content.
More options and events for your base.
More of the AI doing things instead of just waiting around for you to make it happen.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that map sizes feel confined and request larger open worlds for future entries.

citations.review_text:
After 100 hours of survival, State of Decay 2 remains one of the most engaging zombie community-building games out there, though a few structural limitations keep it from true perfection.

What It Does Exceptionally Well:

Brutal Permadeath & Real Tension: Losing a heavily upgraded survivor to an unexpected Feral ambush or Blood Plague infection carries genuine emotional and tactical weight.

Addictive Base & Resource Management: Balancing food rations, ammo, building materials, vehicle fuel, and community morale makes every expedition outside the walls feel necessary and risky.

Satisfying Combat & Atmosphere: Crisp headshots, brutal melee executions, and creeping through pitch-black buildings make scavenging runs intensely immersive.

Why It Loses 2 Points:

Map Size Feels Too Small (-1 Point): While having multiple map options is great, individual territories feel confined fairly quickly once you have established safe driving routes and upgraded vehicles.

Limited Quest Variety (-1 Point): Radiant survivor missions and enclave demands become predictable over time. The core gameplay loop is so enjoyable that it leaves you wishing for deeper, longer story arcs and more complex endgame objectives.

Rating: 8 / 10

A thoroughly enjoyable zombie survival experience with incredible mechanics, held back only by a desire for bigger maps and more diverse questlines to conquer.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe quests and enclave missions as repetitive, predictable chores.

citations.review_text:
After 100 hours of survival, State of Decay 2 remains one of the most engaging zombie community-building games out there, though a few structural limitations keep it from true perfection.

What It Does Exceptionally Well:

Brutal Permadeath & Real Tension: Losing a heavily upgraded survivor to an unexpected Feral ambush or Blood Plague infection carries genuine emotional and tactical weight.

Addictive Base & Resource Management: Balancing food rations, ammo, building materials, vehicle fuel, and community morale makes every expedition outside the walls feel necessary and risky.

Satisfying Combat & Atmosphere: Crisp headshots, brutal melee executions, and creeping through pitch-black buildings make scavenging runs intensely immersive.

Why It Loses 2 Points:

Map Size Feels Too Small (-1 Point): While having multiple map options is great, individual territories feel confined fairly quickly once you have established safe driving routes and upgraded vehicles.

Limited Quest Variety (-1 Point): Radiant survivor missions and enclave demands become predictable over time. The core gameplay loop is so enjoyable that it leaves you wishing for deeper, longer story arcs and more complex endgame objectives.

Rating: 8 / 10

A thoroughly enjoyable zombie survival experience with incredible mechanics, held back only by a desire for bigger maps and more diverse questlines to conquer.

TLDR: State of Okay 🤷‍♂️

I quite like it despite the lack of depth and bugs. And oh boy, are there bugs. And some are annoying as hell.

- For the sake of balance, first I'll echo many of the positives already mentioned by others, such as:
-- the community aspect and micro stories
-- a mild element of "choices matter" from some quests as well as the ever-present possibility of losing a survivor for good
-- graphically holds up well even after all these years, with no major graphical glitches (or none that I've ever noticed)

At the end of the day(break)😏, there's a little bit of something for everyone, enough to make it a fun and brainless (no pun intended) time sink.

[b]However...[/b]

- "Quests" from enclaves are mostly trash, and having to get through a plagued map early on just to do a pointless errand is a dumb, annoying chore.
- Actually, now that I think about it, pretty much everything about "quests" in here is a pointless, annoying chore and a waste of your own community's resources with very few exceptions.
- Doesn't go deep enough into the base building aspect aside from trying to find survivors who have the specializations you need to build this or that.
- Conversely, crafting focus feels like tedium, almost on the verge of factory style micromanagement. This part of the game is tiresome, bothersome, and frankly sometimes ruins the atmosphere. Thankfully, there are far better alternatives.
- Benefits greatly from QoL mods, or else some things just drive me mad. Like vehicle handling. Pun literally intended.
- Monotonous zombie variations, though Lethal mode does make some things more interesting.

citations.review_text:
Intense and edgy play. Good base building. Good replayability. Can feel a little grindy and a little repetitive, and I would love more base customization and options, but well worth the play(s).

A little buggy and I had experiences with freezing, but no more than once every hundred or so hours played. No major issues on Steam. 

I've played lots of hours on both Xbox and Steam and have enjoyed my time.

This game is a horribly janky, hilariously bug filled beautiful mess. It is without a doubt one of the most fun and captivating games I've ever played. Yes it's buggy, but it's not game breaking. 

What I love: 
1. The combat system. The game has so many different weapons, attachments, moves, skills, bonuses and so many more systems that all feed into each other to create a beautiful harmony of interconnected game mechanics. If you're interested, go figure them out; but the best part is, you don't have to. It's not complicated in a "spend more time reading about the game than playing the game" way, it's more depth over complexity. 

2. Stories. The game IS a sandbox survival. But it's not without story. You get long running story lines, mixed up in shorter missions that all come together beautifully. Some maps are more heavily story driven, but it's always a choice. Want to go loot? go for it. Want to go kill stuff? Go for it. Want to summon the onion cutting ninjas? Go for it. (but in all seriousness, some of the stories are 1762 levels of sad). 

3. Community (in game). It's not just about you. It's about putting together the toughest group of improvised badasses the world has ever seen. The serotonin rush from finding that one perfect character is intense. But once again, if that's not your thing the game doesn't push you into it. Yes. there are a few core skills that you really need to have to get the most out of the game, but the rest is personal preference. Now that I think about it, in my opinion this is one of the games biggest strengths; being able to play your way and not getting shoe horned into the playstyle the devs envisioned.  

4. Community (out of game). This game has a large and dedicated community that still plays regularly, and with the sheer amount of choice and options in game, I completely understand why. I've gotten stuck a few times trying to do something my own way, and every time a quick post on reddit or in the forums gets incredibly help…
